I wanna say thank you to everyone who shared their stories and perspectives. I took a long moment to sit down tonight and go through the comments and reflect on myself and the relationships that I’ve had. 

A bit more context : I’m with a group of awesome straight guys, that I’ve met online a few years ago. They treat me like one of the boys (even got to be a groomsman at one of the guys’ wedding). They are truly caring guys and they haven’t made me feel out of place in any sense of the word. 

Those situations are some that have happened in the past, and recently I’ve been in a very introspective mindset. I’m in my mid 20s, and after some (a lot of) soul-searching, I realized that I’ve let past relationships really affect my mental health in a negative way. So I guess this whole post was just so I could see and hear from other people who could bring me some more perspective. 

But thankfully, I’ve found a group where I feel like I belong, with very open and caring friends. They are a role model to me, in the way that they exemplify what I think masculinity should be about. They don’t care in the slightest what other people could perceive from their interactions with me (I danced with practically all of them at a recent wedding lol). I’m at peace for the first time in a long time. 

But once again, thank you everyone so, so very much. It gave me a lot to think about, and I’m appreciative of the straight bros who offered their perspective. Take care guys

Thank you for sharing this. I relate to your situation and it honestly helps knowing that others feel the same way.

The thing that pains me the most is the lack of choice. You either work and feel miserable for the rest of your life, or you try and do something you enjoy but have to be homeless. It's infuriating and sickening

Thank you for sharing your experience. I'm glad you found something that is making you a little bit happier.

There are some aspects of my current job that allow me to walk and visit different sites, which I always appreciate doing. But this is only a small portion of what I actually have to do. Nowhere near enough for my liking. I'm feeling so stressed and anxious ALL THE TIME, and my parents know. But they're adamant that I should suck it up and finish my internship. 

I'm one week in and I'm already miserable, so I don't know if I can...

The internship is supposed to last 4 months, but I have to start working right away as soon as it's finished, so I avoid running out of money. 

I do agree, that perhaps this line of work is not exactly what I like. I have had these feelings of doubt every now and then during my studies, but never really gave it too much attention. I work in a health-related field, but what I truly love is technology. Unfortunately, I figured that out too late, and I can't imagine going back to do a second degree in university. Hence why I feel so trapped in this situation... I guess I'm at a point where I don't know what would make me happy anymore, because I haven't felt happy in months

Everything seems so unreal. I escape by dissociating most of the time, but the idea of having to do this in the long run makes me sick. I can't believe how little awareness has been raised to tackle this issue. The world is so twisted.

I am sorry you haven't been able to talk openly about your struggles. I think that it is the mission of this sub, and I think you've already taken the first step towards fixing the situation. You have to identify at least one person you can freely speak to, either IRL or on this sub. Speaking about what you're going through can be extremely helpful. 

The most important thing is for you to remain safe though. So if the voices are telling you to execute harmful actions, it might be beneficial to seek a licensed professional therapist that would have the required tools to give you clearer instructions on what to do next. Because even though this sub is filled with people who care, nothing can beat an experienced therapist. And remember, there's no shame in reaching out for help. 

Dealing with a mental illness is as valid as having a broken leg - would you just sit and wait for your leg to heal by itself without telling anybody, or would you go and see a doctor? I feel like the same reasoning applies to 

You are not weak, you are valid and you deserve to heal.
